subject: Admin activity exports — transparency checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Elena Martos <elena.martos@novusbiotech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novusbiotech.com, auditor@auditplus.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity logging details + SIG questionnaire

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking our security intake call last week. As we begin the SIG/SOC2 evidence collection, I need a concise view of what Redwood records for admin/operator activity and the export options we can use for evidence handoff. Our auditors have a short checklist — can you confirm the following items so we can map to our control owners?

- Which admin actions are recorded (create/delete user, role changes, API key events, model pin/rollout, config changes, login/auth events)? Please call out any higher-sensitivity actions.
- For each event, what fields are present (actor id/email, timestamp with TZ, IP, request id, previous_state, new_state, request_payload)?
- Retention defaults and configurable retention windows (per-tenant or org-level).
- Export delivery options: on-demand snapshot, incremental delta, streaming (webhook), SFTP, HTTPS pull, signed manifest, checksum approach.
- Redaction controls: PII masking, sampling, or scoped exports.
- Format(s) available: JSONL, Parquet, compressed tarball, and manifest schema.

Attached is the SIG questionnaire we received (SIG_questionnaire_v3.xlsx) — several items map to admin activity. If possible please provide a sample manifest and an example record or two (redacted).

We’d like to review this internally by Thursday and then book a 30-minute call for Friday to finalize the handoff approach.

Thanks,
Elena Martos
Head of Security Programs
NovusBiotech

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a high-level summary; I also attached a redacted sample manifest and two example JSONL records (minimal PII). Happy to walk through live on Friday.

What we log (high level):
- Identity & access events: user creation, deletion, role grants/revokes, API key create/rotate/revoke.
- Operator actions: model deploy/pin/rollback, config updates to routes/quotas, cache invalidation, and schema changes.
- Authentication & sessions: successful/failed logins (SSO/OIDC), token issuance, refresh, altitude of MFA events.
- Administrative telemetry: grant escalations, delegation changes, emergency access activations.

Event fields included (standardized):
- event_id (UUID)
- timestamp (RFC3339 with offset)
- tenant_id / org_id
- actor (internal_id, email where available)
- actor_role (console|api|service_account)
- event_type (verb/resource)
- source_ip (if applicable)
- request_id / correlation_id
- previous_state (JSON diff)
- new_state (JSON diff)
- raw_payload (truncated, base64 if binary)
- severity / result (success|error)

Retention & scoping:
- Hosted default retention: 13 months for admin audit events.
- For Dedicated/Private customers retention is configurable by contract (options: 90d, 1y, 2y, 7y).
- We support org-level retention overrides and a legal-hold flag to freeze retention for specific org_ids.

Export formats and delivery:
- On-demand snapshot: JSONL or Parquet + gzipped tarball.
- Incremental delta: JSONL stream segmented by time-window (hour/day) with sequence numbers.
- Streaming: signed webhook push (mutual TLS) for near realtime pull.
- Delivery transports: SFTP (key auth), HTTPS presigned URL (GET with signed query), or S3-compatible PUT with pre-signed policy.
- Each bundle includes SHA256 checksums and an attestable manifest.jsonl (schema versioned).

PII & redaction controls:
- We provide export-time redaction rules (field-level masking, suppression by regex, and pseudonymization).
- Sampling/export-scope: tenant-only slices, time-boxed windows, or role-scoped (e.g., exclude verbose payloads from service accounts unless requested).

Operational SLAs and verification:
- Standard evidence handoff SLA: 3 business days for on-demand snapshots. Expedited (24h) available with service commitment.
- We include manifest signing (RSA-2048) and HMAC checksums.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach a redacted sample manifest (sample-admin-manifest.jsonl) and two redacted JSONL records after a quick scrub.
2) Confirm whether you need Parquet or JSONL for ingest; auditors often prefer JSONL for raw proofs.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call Friday 10:00–10:30 PT to review final export window and redaction policy.

If you want, Ben can chime in on the cryptographic attestation and manifest signing process.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

-- attachments: sample-admin-manifest.jsonl (jsonl, 5KB), example-record-1.jsonl (jsonl, 1.2KB), example-record-2.jsonl (jsonl, 1.0KB)

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity logging details + SIG questionnaire

Elena / Kim —

Wanted to add a couple of engineering clarifications that come up frequently with customers and auditors:

- Sequence & ordering: our JSONL exports include a monotonic sequence number per-tenant and event.timestamp. Consumers can validate ordering by sequence and checksum.
- Snapshot consistency: on-demand snapshots are point-in-time consistent for admin streams (we freeze writes for a 30s window to ensure manifest consistency).
- Jurisdictional export: for customers requiring EU-only exports we can materialize exports in an EU region and apply geo-redaction rules.

About redaction: we avoid altering the event_id or timestamp (these are canonical). PII fields (email, phone, IP) can be pseudonymized with a reversible tokenization key that you control (KMS-backed). We log key-usage meta events so auditors can verify tokenization ops.

Operational notes for your procurement team: if you request incremental delta via SFTP we’ll provide a signed weekly manifest plus per-file checksums and an optional GPG signature (if you require PGP transfer attestations).

If Novus needs a short acceptance test, we can expose a 48-hour sandbox export with a sample tenant so your auditors can ingest and validate the manifest schema.

-Karthik
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
